clue.text: Good man that's married a woman in hospital?

indicators.note: the married woman's pieces are placed in the middle of the word for hospital

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a hospital
Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about which good fellow wed a woman while she lay in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good man' alludes to the parable of the Good Samaritan; 'hospital' looks like the scene of the wedding but supplies the short form for a sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable, a Good Samaritan is any kind person who helps a stranger in need.

clue.text: Cordial husband getting into singular difficulty

indicators.note: the husband's letter gets into the gap between the singular letter and the word for difficulty

parts.note: S abbreviates singular in grammar
rub means a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A friendly spouse finds himself in an awkward spot of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like an adjective (friendly) but is a noun: a shrub is a fruit cordial or syrup drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is an old-fashioned drink made from fruit juice, sugar and vinegar or spirits, a kind of cordial.

clue.text: Producing euphoria? Dizzy Gillespie certainly didn't!

definitions.meaning: something astonishing or psychedelic that sends you into a high
the jazz trumpeter, famous for his ballooning cheeks, never objected to puffing into his horn

explanation.surface: Was the jazz great's music a source of ecstasy? He clearly loved playing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the phrase as 'didn't mind' + 'blowing': Gillespie happily blew his trumpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so exciting it overwhelms the senses, a sixties slang term for psychedelic experience.

clue.text: Check on general feeling

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in business letters
the pulse of a nation is its general mood or feeling

explanation.surface: A request to gauge the mood of the public.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to check or drive it back.

clue.text: Labour, say, undertaken by char fixes social gathering

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece taken under another sits below it

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
Labour is one example of a political party

explanation.surface: Labour gets its catering from a cleaning lady who arranges a reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'char' looks like a cleaning lady but is slang for tea; Labour is a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon get-together where tea and cakes are served.

clue.text: Pooter's criticism of inferior wine?

definitions.meaning: Charles Pooter is the self-important clerk who writes the Grossmiths' comic diary of an insignificant man
a thin wine is said to lack body, so a critic might grumble that there is none

explanation.surface: What a fussy diarist might say about a cheap bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Pooter, of the Victorian comic novel The Diary of a Nobody, is the person who counts for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of no importance, which Pooter is in the title of his famous diary.

clue.text: Orders to bury last of the remains

indicators.note: the order word buries a letter by holding it inside

parts.note: bids are offers or commands, as in doing someone's bidding

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word 'the' is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for interring the final scraps of a body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a noun for a corpse but is a verb meaning stays; 'to bury' puts E inside BIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bide is to stay or wait, so bides is a verb meaning stays.

clue.text: Florid ornamentation originally seen in sailing vessel

indicators.note: the first letter is seen inside the name of the ship

parts.note: a barque is a three-masted sailing ship

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of ornamentation

explanation.surface: Elaborate decoration first noticed on an old sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Florid ornamentation' reads as one phrase but only 'Florid' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroque style is highly ornate and extravagant, so florid.

clue.text: Welshman I notice needs a lift

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the words makes them read from bottom to top

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement, a notice

explanation.surface: A Welsh fellow realises he needs a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs a lift' turns I + AD upwards to read DAI.
explanation.definitionFit: Dai, short for David, is a stock Welsh first name, used in crosswords for any Welshman.

clue.text: Arab territory rebuilding hospital and kids' home

indicators.note: rebuilding means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs
the word kids, taken as written

explanation.surface: A Gulf state reconstructs a hospital and a children's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A land ruled by a sheikh, as in the Arab world.

clue.text: Period preceding career at university

parts.note: to career is to run headlong
UP means in residence at a university, as in going up to Oxford

explanation.surface: Time before a student dashes around campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is a British usage: you go up to Oxford or Cambridge and come down at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The run-up is the time leading to an event, such as an election.

clue.text: Fruit popular in continental inn

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the French word for an inn

parts.note: an auberge is a French inn
IN means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A dish that goes down well at a French hostelry.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubergine (eggplant) is botanically a fruit, a berry of the nightshade family.

clue.text: Painting in Paris that a king accepts with breakfast?

indicators.note: the whole string of pieces accepts the word for 'with' into its middle

parts.note: Bubbles is Millais's painting of a boy blowing soap bubbles, famous from a soap advertisement
AND can mean with, as in fish and chips
que is French for that
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A French work of art which a monarch takes alongside his morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubbles is a Millais painting famous from a Pears soap advert. Bubble and squeak is a British dish of fried leftover potato and cabbage, often eaten at breakfast, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A fry-up of leftover vegetables, served as a breakfast example, so the query marks it.

clue.text: Board coach, ignoring Republican artiste

parts.note: to board a vehicle is to enter it

indicators.note: ignoring means a letter of the coach word is left out

parts.note: a trainer coaches athletes

explanation.surface: Getting on the bus without the Republican performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board coach' looks like boarding a bus; 'coach' is TRAINER, which loses an R.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer such as a singer or comic who amuses an audience.

clue.text: A Utopian writer races round to see Cupid

parts.note: Sir Thomas More wrote Utopia
the TT races are the Isle of Man motorcycle Tourist Trophy
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A Renaissance author hurries about to meet the god of love.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the motorcycle race series held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a little cupid or cherub figure in Italian art.

clue.text: Rook leaves wild churchyard in Franz Ferdinand's territory

indicators.note: wild says the churchyard letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A bird flies off from an overgrown burial ground on an Austrian prince's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook leaves' takes one R from CHURCHYARD; 'wild' rearranges what remains. 'Rook' looks like the bird but is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Ferdinand was an archduke of Austria, and an archduke's domain is so named.

clue.text: Dealt a heavy blow, as an earl may be

definitions.meaning: a '... earl' is a traditional phrase, earls being invested with a sword belt

explanation.surface: Struck hard, much as a noble lord might be.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'belted earl' is an old British phrase from the ceremony of girding a new earl with a sword belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck forcefully; also wearing a ceremonial belt, as earls traditionally did.

clue.text: Make off with list showing engine component

parts.note: to fly is to flee or make off
a ship that lists heels over to one side

explanation.surface: Run away taking a register that reveals a machine part.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy rotating wheel in an engine that stores momentum and smooths its running.

clue.text: Easy task, trapping large seal

indicators.note: the easy-task word holds a letter caught inside it

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy
L is the abbreviation for large on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Catching a big marine mammal proves straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal' looks like the animal but is the verb, as in sealing a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal is to settle or confirm it, as a seal does.

clue.text: Break into marriage feast venue, using metal bar

indicators.note: the metal breaks into the venue's name, sitting within it

parts.note: Cana is where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding feast
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Gatecrashing a wedding reception with a crowbar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal bar' looks like one item; 'metal' is TIN and 'bar' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a bar or tavern in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: It's used to pluck fruit outside court in mid-term

indicators.note: the fruit sits outside the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: the court letters go inside the middle of the term word
mid points to the centre letters of the word term

explanation.surface: A tool for picking fruit around the court during the half-term break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-term' gives only the centre of TERM; 'pluck' suggests picking fruit, but a plectrum plucks strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A plectrum is the small pick a guitarist uses on the strings.

clue.text: Turn in a clue devised for waterproof garment

indicators.note: the turn word goes inside the rearranged letters
devised means the letters are composed afresh in a new order

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Writing a crossword clue for a rain jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges A CLUE to CAULE; 'Turn' looks like the anagram signal but is the word for a go.
explanation.definitionFit: A cagoule is a lightweight hooded rain jacket.

clue.text: Requesting a film — Goldfinger to begin with

parts.note: a skin is a thin film or layer, as on custard

indicators.note: to begin with points to the first letter of the word Goldfinger

explanation.surface: Asking for a Bond movie, starting with Goldfinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie (Goldfinger is a Bond film) but means a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for something is making a request.

clue.text: Invite disaster — practise DIY in churchyard!

definitions.meaning: do-it-yourself in a burial ground would mean making your own burial pit

explanation.surface: Courting ruin by doing your own handiwork among the tombstones.
explanation.walkthrough: DIY is do-it-yourself home improvement; the literal reading has you excavating your own plot.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for acting in a way that causes your own ruin.

clue.text: Live in England's borders, like some seals

indicators.note: the living verb sits in between the borders of England
borders means the first and last letters of the country's name

parts.note: to live is to be, and we are

explanation.surface: Residing near the boundaries of England, as certain marine animals do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' is the verb to exist (ARE), not to reside.
explanation.definitionFit: Eared seals, such as sea lions, have small external ear flaps.

clue.text: Firm takes on case out east involving perceptive thinking

indicators.note: the firm word takes on the rest, joining it at its end

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: out means the east letter is taken away from the case

parts.note: the genitive is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: A company takes on a lawsuit abroad that calls for real insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a legal action but is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the mental processes of knowing and reasoning.

clue.text: It may be applied to locks on rising

definitions.text: It may be applied to locks

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A substance put on locks as they go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' are hair, not door locks. In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair gel is a styling product put on hair, poetically called locks.

clue.text: Some frightful narrowing of a bone

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some alarming constriction of a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnar describes things relating to the ulna, a forearm bone.

clue.text: Unknown male leaving European island for Crimean port

parts.note: Y is an unknown in algebra

indicators.note: leaving means the male letter departs from the island's name

parts.note: Malta is a Mediterranean island nation in Europe

explanation.surface: A stranger leaves a Mediterranean island to sail for a Black Sea harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta is a resort port on the Crimean peninsula, site of the 1945 conference.

clue.text: Bloomer made by former commander without staff

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the commander word goes around the other

parts.note: GEN is the abbreviation for general, a commander
old means former, as in an old flame
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: An error committed by an ex-officer lacking his team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a plant that blooms; 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a flowering plant with yellow sprays, so something that blooms.
